label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
@Tolu_Aspirant Tolu, I’m Amaka. I’m in Biology 100L and I wanted Medicine. So I’m the person your question is for, and I’ll talk to you straight, no plastic advice.

First, breathe. What you’re feeling is normal. When I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. For like two months my mum was still telling people in church that I was doing Medicine, and I had to beg her to stop. So I know that cry you’re crying. It’s not small.

But let me give you the real gist about transfer, because this is where people confuse others. I scored 251 in JAMB, applied Medicine and Surgery, and they offered me Biology in a federal uni here in Lagos. Our level adviser told us that to move to MBBS after 100L, you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5 AND there must be space. Both. Not one. The adviser said last year about 6 people got moved in from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 applied. So you see why I can’t tell you “just accept and transfer, it’s automatic.” It is not. Kingsley saying transfer is a myth is not true, people do move. But favour saying “just read hard” is too simple. Reading hard is part, but there is space, cut-offs, and your school’s process. I’m inside it, my CGPA after first semester is 4.31, not 4.5, and I’m still trying. So it’s possible, but it’s competitive.

Also, 268 is a good JAMB score, but it alone doesn’t establish eligibility for transfer. You need to meet your school’s Medicine cut-offs in JAMB and post-UTME too. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or your post-UTME score. You have to check both. If your post-UTME is not up to their Medicine cut-off, the transfer talk may not even start. So before you make a decision, go to your faculty/department and ask the exact transfer rules for your own school. Don’t just trust forum people, including me. Ask them: what CGPA, what cut-off, how many spaces, when do people apply, what is the process. Get it from the source.

Now, about Biology itself. 100L courses are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people, honestly. There are also small expenses: my lab coat was 6,500 naira, dissecting kit 9k, practical manual extra. Nothing too crazy, but it adds up. In my first BIO practical we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted. I was fine. That day I realised I actually like this thing. I’m enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. So Biology is not a bad course. It’s just that many of us came in with Medicine in our head, so we see it as a consolation prize. It’s not useless.

But this is the part I want you to be honest with yourself about. Ask yourself: do I want Medicine, or do I just want to be called “doctor”? Because if it’s for your parents, or for the title, that’s a different thing. If it’s truly Medicine, then you have to decide if you’re ready to fight for the transfer or rewrite. If you accept Biology, don’t accept it thinking transfer is guaranteed. Accept it because you can give Biology a chance while you try, or because you’re okay with the possibility that transfer may not work. Don’t use Biology as a waiting room and then be miserable for years if transfer doesn’t happen.

And if you’re thinking of rewriting, hear this too. Staying at home is not as easy as people say. favour is right about that. I have a secondary school classmate, Ifeoma. She rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she’s still at home. I’m not saying this to scare you, that’s just the reality. Rewriting is not wrong if you are ready. But it is not a small thing. You need to be honest about whether you can handle another year at home, another JAMB, another post-UTME, and the uncertainty. If you can, fine. If you cannot, don’t let anybody push you.

So my advice: in these two weeks, go and ask the department the exact rules. Check your school’s Medicine cut-offs and your post-UTME. Talk to your dad and your aunty with facts, not just fear. Then decide. If you accept, go in with your eyes open and work for the 4.5 and above, but also let yourself enjoy Biology small. If you rewrite, go in with a plan, not just because your aunty said so. Whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world. I know it feels like it now, but it’s not. You have time. Just don’t let forum people, including me, make the final decision for you. We can only tell you our experience. The decision is yours. Sending you strength, Tolu. You’ll be okay.
